transcript.text: Bosch WTN85201GB condenser dryer not drying properly anymore, clothes still damp after 2 hrs. any ideas

A condenser dryer that suddenly leaves clothes damp is usually an airflow/condensation issue rather than the drum itself. Try these in order:

1. Clean both lint filters thoroughly
• Remove the door lint filter(s), open them if they split apart, and remove all fluff.
• Rinse under warm water if they look coated with detergent/fabric-softener residue, then dry fully before refitting. A thin invisible film can seriously restrict airflow.

2. Empty the water container
• Even if it is not full, empty and refit it firmly. Check the little valve/connection area is not blocked.

3. Clean the lower filter/condenser area
• Your WTN85201GB may have a lower flap/filter arrangement. Follow the machine’s manual for the accessible filter(s).
• Vacuum loose fluff around the opening and clean the filter as instructed.
• Don’t poke tools into, or aggressively wash, an internal condenser that is not designed to be removed—its fins damage easily.

4. Clean the moisture sensors
• Inside the drum, usually near the door opening, are two metal strips. Wipe them with a cloth dampened with white vinegar or mild washing-up liquid, then wipe dry.
• Fabric-softener residue can make the dryer think laundry is dry and stop/behave incorrectly.

5. Check the load and programme
• Dry a normal-sized load spun at least 1,000–1,400 rpm. Very wet laundry, an overloaded drum, or one bulky item can remain damp.
• Try a timed warm-dry programme rather than an automatic sensor programme. Use a couple of damp towels for the test.
• Cotton “Cupboard Dry” programmes can genuinely take around 2 hours, especially in a cool room, but clothes should not still be notably wet at the end.

6. Check whether it is actually heating
• After 10–15 minutes on a timed warm programme, open the door briefly: the drum and laundry should feel distinctly warm.
• If it is cool or only barely warm, likely causes include a failed heater, thermostat/thermal cut-out, wiring fault, or control-board fault. That needs an appliance engineer.
• If it is hot but still damp, restricted airflow, clogged filter/condenser path, or a condensate pump/collection problem is more likely.

7. Room conditions
• Leave some space around the dryer and ventilate the room. Condenser dryers perform poorly in very cold, damp, unventilated rooms.

If cleaning the filters/sensors does not help and a timed programme is not producing proper heat, stop using it until checked—repeated long cycles can overheat components. Bosch service or an independent white-goods engineer would be appropriate; give them the full E‑Nr from the door frame, not just WTN85201GB.

Door filters had fluff and a waxy film, scrubbed them under the tap until water went through. The bottom-front condenser I'd never cleaned, the front was matted with lint, but it rinsed clean with the shower head. Vacuumed fluff from the slot behind it, wiped the dull drum sensor bars with vinegar. It was hot inside the drum after 20 min, load was normal at 1200 spin, and the container only had a little water before. After all that, a test cycle dried in about 100 mins and the container was nearly full.

That strongly suggests it was blocked airflow/poor condenser performance, and you’ve fixed it.

The key signs are:

• Drum was hot: heater is working.
• Water container nearly full: it is now extracting moisture properly.
• Load dried in ~100 minutes: normal territory for a condenser dryer on a standard cotton load, depending on programme and fabric thickness.
• Matted condenser front and waxy lint filters: both would have severely reduced air movement and condensation.

A couple of worthwhile follow-ups:

• Let the door filters dry completely before using them again. Clean them every load, and rinse/degrease them periodically if water starts beading rather than flowing through.
• Clean the lower condenser/filter area regularly—roughly monthly for normal use, more often with pets, towels, or lots of laundry. Follow the Bosch instructions for your specific removable part.
• Avoid excessive fabric softener and dryer sheets, as these cause the waxy filter coating and sensor residue.
• Wipe the sensor bars every few months if automatic programmes start ending early.
• Make sure the dryer has breathing room around it and the room is not extremely cold.

If future loads start taking much longer again despite clean filters, check the condenser area first. But based on that test, it sounds as though the dryer itself is now operating normally.
